questions.stem: Which of the following statements about a Java class is FALSE?

options.text: A class can contain only methods and no fields.
A class can have multiple constructors with different parameter lists.
A class can be declared as abstract to prevent direct instantiation.
A class can contain a static block that runs once when the class is first loaded.

questions.explanation: A class can contain fields (instance variables). The statement claiming it can contain only methods is false. Classes may have both fields and methods.
When `new B()` is called, Java first invokes the superclass constructor `A()` which prints "A". After that, it executes the body of `B()` which prints "B". Thus the combined output is "AB".

questions.stem: Which keyword is used in Java to restrict access to a class member so that it can only be accessed within its own package and subclasses?
questions.explanation: The `protected` keyword allows access within the same package and by subclasses, even if they are in different packages. `private` restricts to the declaring class only, while `public` permits all access.
